tools.name: create_decision
tools.description:
Create a poll, check-in, availability board, or ranking and get a link to share with the group.

Easiest: pass `text` in plain language and SettleIt infers the type and options, e.g. "Dinner: pizza or thai" (poll), "Who's in for bowling Thursday?" (checkin), "Find a time for dinner next week" (avail

tools.name: get_decision
tools.description: Read a decision and its current results: votes and leaders for polls, rankings with points, In/Maybe/Out names for check-ins, and per-slot counts plus best_slot_ids for availability. Also returns the option or slot ids that respond_to_decision needs.

tools.name: respond_to_decision
tools.description:
Record one person's answer, only when that person asked you to. Which fields you need depends on the decision's type (get_decision shows it in `respond.fields`):
- poll: voter_id + option (exact label) or option_id
- ranking: voter_id + order (every option label or id, best first)
- checkin: name +

tools.name: close_decision
tools.description: Stop accepting responses. Results stay visible. Requires the admin_token.

tools.name: reopen_decision
tools.description: Accept responses again after closing (clears an automatic close time that has passed). Requires the admin_token.

tools.name: delete_decision
tools.description: Permanently delete a decision and all its responses. The share link stops working. This cannot be undone, so confirm with the user first. Requires the admin_token.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_decision · Private data: create_decision, respond_to_decision · Public sink: create_decision, delete_decision · Destructive: delete_decision.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_decision · Private data: create_decision, respond_to_decision · Public sink: create_decision, delete_decision · Destructive: delete_decision

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
